diagnosis.primary: Structural design gap: the low-signal guard is INACTIVE for the first warmup_observations=50 updates ('bootstrap window: observe, do not skip'), but the near-zero-signal pathology is present from update 1 (momentum restored from ckpt_97100 + persistently near-zero live gradients of slot_07/08 attention q_proj). During the window every update feeds the ~5e-9 Nesterov matrix into NS4, whose chaotic-bit amplification (forensic: ~20% catastrophic branch per application) produces a stochastic O(0.1) delta. P(crash within 50 observations) ~ 1 - 0.8^50 ~= 99.9%. Observed crash observations across 4 runs: 13, 2, 7, 3.
diagnosis.guard_calibration_is_not_the_fault: would_skip_after_warmup=true: the calibrated ratio line (u_t_rms 5.0e-9 < 0.1*ref 7.0e-9) correctly classifies this tensor as low-signal. If the warmup gate were not suppressing the skip decision, the crash would not have occurred.
diagnosis.secondary_risk_reference_decay: refs update as max(sig, ref*0.999) per active observation: for a persistently near-zero tensor the ref decays toward the ~5e-9 level, dragging ratio_line below the actual signal over time; the ratio test then becomes self-referential and the skip protection erodes even after warmup. Flagged for the next iteration (needs a data-driven recalibration, not an arbitrary threshold).
diagnosis.secondary_risk_floor_units: numerical_floor (6.575e-07) applies to the whole-chunk Frobenius norm, which scales with sqrt(numel): for a 6.55M-element chunk the floor only catches rms < ~8e-11. It never fires for large chunks; the elementwise-rms backstop implied by the spec's 'absolute numerical floor' second line is not what is implemented.
diagnosis.fail_closed_verification: The two-phase design behaved as intended in all 4 runs: no parameter write on violation (PHASE1 fail-closed), rank-consistent verdict (same tensors flagged on both ranks), clean stop with diagnostics, ckpt_97100 remains pristine (no new checkpoint written before crash; cadence 100).
